chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Aamir, from Moalla ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abu Hammad, all together from Al-Washa, from Ahmad ibn A'iz, from Abu Khadeeja Salim ibn Mukram, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who asked us, we gave it to him, and the one who managed without (asking), Allah enriched him.'

key_terms.مَنْ سَأَلَنَا: The one who asked us (the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the Prophet's saying about asking the Ahl al-Bayt and Allah's enrichment?
ai.summary: This hadith, found in the chapter on Contentment (al-Rida) in al-Kafi, underscores the spiritual economy of the Ahl al-Bayt, where their intercession and guidance are contingent upon the supplicant's active seeking (su'al). It reflects the Shia theological principle that divine enrichment is often a response to humble dependence on the Imams, contrasting with the self-sufficiency that may lead to spiritual neglect. The chain of transmission highlights the reliability of the Kufan school of hadith, linking the Prophet directly to Imam al-Sadiq through a robust isnad.
